name: The Culture

population: Humans living inside the Machine's underground settlements
basis: All-age underground-resident scenario allows extensive automatic provision but counts attendants, lecturers, committees and useful communication as work.

name: WALL-E (Axiom before the return to Earth)

name: The Evitable Conflict
population: Human inhabitants of the machine-coordinated world economy

name: Noon Universe (Earth)
population: Human residents of Earth
basis: Human all-age scenario with strong vocational participation: machines remove routine subsistence work but science, education, care, exploration and creative contribution persist.

name: Brave New World (original novel)
population: Humans within the World State's caste order
basis: Engineered adult castes perform assigned work; the all-age scenario allows children and others outside productive roles. Short hours and conditioning are not nonworking statistics.

name: Nineteen Eighty-Four (Oceania)
population: Humans living under Oceania's Party order
basis: All-age scenario under compulsory labor and scarcity; useful Party administration, production, care and informal survival are work, with dependents allowed.

basis: Biological-person all-age scenario retains military, administrative, productive and care work under rejected machine autonomy; no civilian census inferred from war scenes.

name: Foundation and Earth (Solaria after withdrawal)
population: Resident human-descended Solarians, including children denied full ruler status
basis: Coarse editorial estimate of near-total release from routine productive duty; oversight remains possible.

name: The Robots of Dawn (Aurora)
population: Auroran human residents and dependents
basis: Auroran resident-human scenario permits strong technical assistance while retaining professional, creative, scientific and care roles; free robot access does not state how many work.

population: Immortal human bodies and their associated individual or joining minds

population: Human residents, including Labour Company workers and their children

population: Present Utopian human residents, including children

population: Living biological Indiots during the transfer and exercise of machine authority; explicit humanlike population proxy
basis: Only living Indiots during early machine rule are counted. Displacement plausibly leaves many without work, while care and survival roles persist; later extermination is excluded.

name: Return from the Stars (Betrized Earth)
population: The living human population of the depicted Earth
basis: Living-human all-age scenario allows major robot substitution while counting specialists, services, care and chosen useful roles. Robot ratios are not human participation rates.

population: Living biological Luzanian Entians, explicitly used as a humanlike participation proxy
basis: Living Entian all-age proxy scenario under extensive molecular production; humanities, specialist intervention, care and other chosen useful activity still count as work.

name: Voyage from Yesteryear (Chiron)
population: Living human Chironians raised through the colony's robot-supported founding and their descendants
basis: Chiron all-age scenario: robot provision removes wage necessity, while useful art, technology, care and chosen projects continue.

name: The Metamorphosis of Prime Intellect (Cyberlife)
population: Active human persons in the system's shared and private environments; bodily instances do not multiply the population
basis: Active-human-person scenario under removable physical needs; art, science, care and sustained socially useful activity still count. Bodies and copies are not multiplied.

population: Resident humans of the United Welfare States, within the developed-country provision described by the consulted account
basis: The review explicitly describes almost nobody working, beyond merely receiving stipends. This broad all-resident editorial estimate allows substantial uncertainty for the continuing military, services, research and useful voluntary work; no labor-force denominator is silently converted.

name: Erewhon (The machine ban)
population: Living Erewhonian human residents of all ages
basis: Erewhonian all-age scenario retains labor after deliberate machine destruction, including farming, craft and care; dependents and others outside sustained roles remain included.

basis: The depicted families farm and undertake useful household/craft labor despite industrial automation. This coarse all-resident estimate allows for children, age and incapacity; no census or wage-to-work conversion is claimed.

population: Living Ledom residents of all ages, biologically modified human descendants treated as persons
basis: Living Ledom all-age scenario allows effortless necessities while counting education, science, care and creative contribution; no-wage vocabulary does not measure participation.

population: The living residents of Mattapoisett, including children and caregivers
basis: All-age community scenario retains extensive farming, care, making, education and civic contribution. Machines reduce burdens but do not imply low participation.

population: Living Whileawayans of all ages
basis: All-age Whileawayan scenario under strong work obligations; shorter formal hours still count as work, as does caregiving. Conflicting accounts are not a census.

basis: Living demarchic-system all-age scenario allows substantial automatic provision while retaining professions, research, care and civic participation. No inference from absent unemployment mentions.

basis: Active embodied Higher-citizen scenario under rejected commercial economics; useful science, care, governance and chosen roles continue. Long life is not a census.

basis: Active human and human-derived resident scenario permits broad automation-supported leisure but retains engineering, art, care and useful projects; Sophotech task or wealth shares are not participation.

name: Star Trek — Aldea under the Custodian
population: Living biological Aldean residents, used as a humanoid-person comparison proxy

basis: Human Union population scenario under free synthesizer provision; useful careers, research, care and civic contribution remain work even without wages.

population: Living human residents of equipped Motorway cars, with mixed-species neighbors as context
basis: All-age human car-household scenario counts recurring driving, maintenance, care and useful coordination; failure to reach paid jobs does not make those tasks disappear.

population: Living human pioneers while supported by the colony system
basis: Living advance-party scenario assumes most pioneers retain useful setup, farming, maintenance or care roles, consistent with Kezzia’s pollination work; slain and sleeping colonists are excluded.

basis: Active admitted upload-person scenario allows sponsor-funded leisure and counts useful digital creation, technical activity and care-like contribution; suspended users are outside the active denominator.

population: Active human-derived digital persons whose physical bodies have died

name: The Expanse — Earth under Basic Assistance
population: Registered Earth citizens eligible for Basic, including those without employment
basis: Job scarcity and broad Basic use support substantial nonparticipation, reduced by useful informal/care activity; benefit receipt is not treated as no work.

name: Black Mirror — San Junipero’s permanent residents
population: Active human-derived permanent residents
basis: A recreational permanent afterlife strongly suggests high leisure; this broad noncanonical estimate allows many residents to undertake useful chosen work. The depicted couple is not a statistical sample.

population: Living human residents of Sunset City
basis: Retirement and extensive menial-task replacement support a high broad estimate, with room for substantial useful voluntary activity; no exact census is claimed.

name: Pantheon — Maddie’s stellar simulation project
population: Maddie as the continuing active human-derived owner/resident of the outer project
basis: In the explicitly one-resident project scope, Maddie undertakes ongoing useful reconstruction/research. This is a role-based scope judgment, not a universe-wide census.

name: Expelled from Paradise — DEVA’s memory-ranked digital society
population: Active human-derived citizens using DEVA resources
basis: Contribution-ranked resources incentivize ongoing useful activity, including digital security and administration; active persons, not archived or suspended files, form the denominator.
